title: KPI accumulator and governance sprint pulse
content:
Purpose:
This working document captures a compact, rolling KPI accumulator and a governance sprint pulse intended for short-cycle launches and feature rollouts. It is designed to sit alongside the standard release playbooks but focuses on:
- single-pane KPI ingestion across product ops, SRE, and support
- a governance ladder for quick decisions tied to metric thresholds
- a three-day pulse cadence for early-launch stabilization and triage

Scope and use cases:
1) Early beta and internal canaries (0–10k requests/day) — fast feedback, low blast radius.
2) Controlled public beta (10k–100k requests/day) — capacity triggers and throttles enabled.
3) Ramp to scale (>100k requests/day) — coordinate with Dedicated and infra SRE.

How the accumulator works (practical):
- Each owner (product, infra, support) writes a 1-line signal into the accumulator sheet daily during first 72 hours. The accumulator merges: latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost burn rate, onboarding conversion, and rejection/QA flags.
- Signals are prioritized: Severity A (stop+rollback candidate), B (mitigate w/ config), C (monitor).
- Thresholds are configured per launch profile (beta / pilot / scale). See threshold table below.

Threshold & Governance ladder (example values — teams tune by launch):
- Latency P95 > 1200ms (A) — immediate rollback decision owner: infra lead
- Error spike > 2x baseline and >= 0.5% absolute (A) — triage owner: SRE + product
- Token cost per 1k requests > 30% expected (B) — cost mitigation owner: product-ops + optimize team
- Model quality regressions (measured by eval suite holdouts delta > 3% BLEU/metric) (B) — Model owner: applied-ml
- Customer-reported severity 1 (SLA breach) (A) — escalation: CS lead + account owner

Three-day pulse cadence (first 72 hours recommended):
Day 0 (launch window) — preflight checklist, staff runway, oncall notifier, red-team smoke tests. 1-hour cadence for first 6 hours.
Day 1 — KPI accumulator snapshot at 09:00, 13:00, 17:00. Small-batch canary assessments at 12:00 and 16:00.
Day 2 — KPI accumulator snapshot at 09:00 and 15:00. Decision sync at 17:00 with rollback posture if any Severity A unresolved.
Day 3 — reduce cadence to twice/day; prepare handoff to weekly ops rhythm if stable.

Sample accumulator row format (text capture, one-line per owner):
- timestamp | owner | signal-tags | P50ms | P95ms | error_rate% | token_cost_delta% | quality_delta% | action_taken | notes/links
Example: 2025-01-20T09:00Z | Lena M. | infra,latency | 210 | 890 | 0.15 | +5 | 0 | scaled pool +20% | https://jira.redwood.com/browse/PROD-4123

Decision matrix (short):
- If any Severity A appears: convene 15-min emergency triage, meet in #launch-ops, pre-declared rollback owner has 30 minutes to implement safe rollback.
- If multiple B-level signals persist across two snapshots: enact mitigations (scaling, model-quantization toggle, traffic shed) and escalate to weekly exec readout if unresolved by end of day.
- C-level items logged into playbook backlog for follow-up in next sprint.

Owner roles and simple responsibilities:
- Product-ops (owner: Lena Morales) — accumulator keeper, rolls daily snapshot notes, chairs Day-1 sync.
- Infra/SRE (owner: Evan Gupta) — latency & error triage, rollback executor for infra-level fixes.
- Applied ML (owner: Priya Nair) — model quality signals, rollback options for model variant switching.
- Customer Success (owner: Tomás Alvarez) — customer-impact signals and account-level escalation.
- Optimize (owner: Riley Park) — token-cost mitigations, batching/caching recommendations.

Short checklist (preflight, 30–60 minutes before launch):
- Routing: fallback model variants configured and smoke-tested
- Observability: P95, P50, error_rate charts wired to accumulator; dashboards shared with #launch-ops
- Rollback: validated and rehearsed rollback runbook exists with owner and permissions
- Staff: oncall + 2 extra engineers for first 12 hours; CS on standby for top accounts
- Quotas: rate limits and traffic-shaping policies are in place
- Cost controls: temporary caps configured for token spend if pilot exceeds forecast

Post-launch artifacts to produce (Day 3–7):
- Consolidated accumulator snapshot (CSV export + highlights)
- Incident timeline for any Severity A events (owner: SRE)
- Lessons learned quick memo (owner: product-ops) with 3 follow-up actions assigned to next sprint

Open questions / TODOs for this doc (work-in-progress):
- finalize thresholds per launch-profile (need product + infra signoff)
- wire a Confluence macro to embed accumulator CSV and auto-refresh
- test auto-notification to oncall Slack group when Severity A detected (PROD-4123 ticket)

Quick links and references:
- Launch governance model (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PROD/launch-governance-model
- Accumulator prototype sheet: https://sheets.redwood.com/d/1-example-accum-sheet
- Emergency rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/rollback-playbook

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact so teams can copy the accumulator into a shared sheet per launch. Suggest piloting on the next internal canary and iterating thresholds based on real signals.
- If you want to own a threshold value for a profile (beta/pilot/scale), add your name under collaborators and propose a numeric value in the comments section below.

-- Lena Morales
product-ops
